summary.text: Tim Burchett is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 2nd District, a Knoxville native and former small-business owner who served in the Tennessee House and Senate and as Knox County mayor before winning the seat in 2018. He serves on the Oversight and Government Reform, Foreign Affairs, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is seeking re-election in November 2026.

paragraphs.text: Tim Burchett was born in Knoxville, Tennessee, in 1964, and grew up there, attending Bearden High School, from which he graduated in 1982.
He earned a bachelor's degree in education from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, in 1988.
According to his official biography, he worked as a businessman and started a small business before entering the state legislature.
Burchett served in the Tennessee House of Representatives from 1994 to 1998 and in the Tennessee Senate from 1998 to 2010.

He was then Knox County mayor from 2010 to 2018, a tenure during which, his official biography says, his administration built new schools, launched infrastructure projects, and paid down debt without raising taxes.
He won the November 2018 general election for the 2nd District seat and took office in January 2019.

In the 119th Congress Burchett serves on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency, as well as on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

His official biography says that, of the bills he sponsored or cosponsored, three in the 117th Congress (including the PAWS for Veterans Therapy Act) and six in the 118th Congress were signed into law.
He lives in the Gibbs community of Knox County with his wife, Kelly, and their daughter, Isabel, according to the same biography.
